title: Cahokia reaches a major urban peak
summary: Cahokia near the Mississippi River became a large centre of the Mississippian world. Earthen mounds, surrounding villages and agricultural settlement reveal a complex regional society at its eleventh- and twelfth-century peak.

claims.text: Cahokia near the Mississippi River became a large centre of the Mississippian world. Earthen mounds, surrounding villages and agricultural settlement reveal a complex regional society at its eleventh- and twelfth-century peak.
Peak-period range, not all occupation of the site.

Monumental earthworks provide evidence of collective labour and political organization. Cahokia belongs within Indigenous North American history well before sustained European colonization; population estimates remain approximate.
